A continuous tail-eigenvector mixture crosses |<Tx,x>|=q while retaining ||Tx||>1, giving strict q-radius inflation. For ||T||<=1 the norm bound meets an essential-tail lower bound. The explicit square-summation identity (5) proves the q=1 boundary threshold sqrt(2). All quantifiers, endpoint restrictions, and infinite limits are analytic, independent of finite tests.

value.rationale: The finding classifies contractivity by a scalar q-radius equality across the entire ideal of compact perturbations of a fixed essential isometry, simultaneously for all 0<q<1. The exact failure at q=1 is witnessed by a natural one-edge rank-one perturbation with sharp sqrt(2) boundary. This yields nontrivial infinite-dimensional rigidity beyond finite or periodic shift tables, with potential use as a contraction test.
